PHYSICS — MOCK EXAM #19
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: PHYSICS
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. newton (N)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. watt (W)

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

3. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Producers

4. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Nitrogen gas only

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Photoelectric effect? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Photoelectric effect.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Photoelectric effect.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Photoelectric effect.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Photoelectric effect.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Satellites? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Satellites.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Satellites.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Satellites.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Satellites.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Transistors? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Transistors.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Transistors.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Transistors.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Transistors.

8. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Removing all vegetation

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mains electricity? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Mains electricity.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mains electricity.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mains electricity.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mains electricity.

10. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Milk souring

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Thin lenses? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Thin lenses.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Thin lenses.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Thin lenses.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Thin lenses.

13. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Floating and Sinking? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Floating and Sinking.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Floating and Sinking.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Floating and Sinking.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Floating and Sinking.

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Circular motion? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Circular motion.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Circular motion.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Circular motion.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Circular motion.

16. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water always increases oxygen

17. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

18. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Dynamics? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Dynamics.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Dynamics.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Dynamics.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Dynamics.

19. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electromagnetic induction? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electromagnetic induction.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electromagnetic induction.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electromagnetic induction.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Electromagnetic induction.

20. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Quantity of Heat? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Quantity of Heat.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Quantity of Heat.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Quantity of Heat.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Quantity of Heat.

21. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
22. In three clear sentences, explain Quantity of Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Thin lenses and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Photoelectric effect and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Electromagnetic induction and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Mains electricity and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

27. In three clear sentences, explain Transistors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

28. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

29. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Satellites and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
